newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: Spain's debt market ended slightly higher on Monday amid lacklustre trade and little news.
But dealers said they expected trade to be brisker tomorrow as expectations of a declining January CPI, due on February 13, should boost prices at the short end of the yield curve.
"Spain is the only place in Europe where it's interesting to bet on the steepening of the yield curve," said Thierry Loiseau, dealer at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.
He added that if January CPI came in as expected and declined to 3.0 percent year-on-year from 3.2 in December, a cut in interest rates could be approved quickly.
"If we see a number around 3.0 percent, or less, the market will start betting on a rate cut," said Loiseau.
The Bank of Spain will announce the results of its regular repurchase tender on Friday, the day after the CPI data.
"It seems likely that the Bank of Spain will cut rates by 25 basis points to 5.75 pct on the back of the release at Friday's operation," San Paolo Bank said in a client research report.
Spain's yield curve was steepening already on Monday, especially in the five-year segment, in anticipation.
The 10-year spread over Bunds changed benchmark bonds. With the new bonds, the spread closed at around 124 basis points.
